I.4  Web Repair Evaluation Protocol

The recorded case in Figure 18 illustrates browser feedback and code repair. A controlled repair comparison additionally fixes the issue set, starting patch, Coding Agent, test generator, adjudicator, budgets, and protected acceptance conditions. Role-specific information remains separate even when roles share model weights.

Each assigned issue begins with the nominated defect reproduced. Before a new condition or patch is tested, browser storage, account/backend data, service-worker state, and external fixtures are restored. Intentional stateful test dependencies remain explicit. Reports bind the build, reset state, test item, and attempt. Only evidence-supported product discrepancies justify a repair.

Acceptance uses the common assigned issue set as its denominator, retaining tester noncompletion. Infrastructure-invalid attempts follow the same bounded rerun rule, and unresolved issues remain in the results. Final acceptance runs the submitted patch from a protected clean state outside the repair loop, with its outputs withheld from further revision.

Appendix J OSWorld 2.0 Execution Cases

These cases follow NorthCUA through selected decisions in complete desktop tasks. Counts refer to model decisions, each of which can issue multiple tools. Agent callouts summarize recorded decisions for readability.

The pair in Figure 28 has identical requests but different dataset revisions. The earlier run records unavailable OCR, while the later run uses it. The case follows source selection and verification in each execution.

J.1  Preserving a Delivery Constraint Across Long Contexts

The photo-delivery task in Figure 42 requires the agent to reconcile invoices against bank payments, identify two clients’ photos, and send different deliveries. Sarah has paid her $800 invoice in full and should receive her complete gallery. Emily has paid $250 of a $500 invoice and should receive a watermarked solo-indoor preview with a balance reminder. The difficulty is carrying this distinction through image preparation and email composition after the original banking interaction leaves recent context.

After exact-name payment matching, the agent records Emily’s outstanding $250 and preview-only rule at decision 46. The compacted input at decision 150 retains both and the unfinished delivery checks, carrying the payment constraint beyond the earlier interaction history.

At decision 233, two action-marked historical screenshots identify the attachment click and selected PNG, while the clean current frame shows the file attached to Emily’s draft. The agent sends the message and checks its sent copy at decision 236, confirming the preview and $250 reminder. A final image inspection confirms the watermark, and the 243-decision attempt receives full credit. Notes and compaction preserve the constraint, while the bounded image window exposes the current attachment state.

J.2  Using a Terminal Through the GUI

Figure 43 follows a 3D course-logo task requiring Bauhaus 93 text, a 120-frame rotation, and a 960 ×\times 540 WebM video at 24 fps inside Impress. To control scene settings and automate repeated rendering, the agent opens a terminal through GUI keypresses and types commands. Its exposed tools are desktop actions and notes, and the task permits terminal and application-console use.

After opening a terminal at decision 3 to identify fonts, the agent builds the scene in Blender’s scripting workspace. When direct video export rejects WEBM and FFMPEG settings, it renders 120 PNG frames and encodes them with terminal-based ffmpeg using VP9 at 24 fps, preserving the 960 ×\times 540 resolution. Separating rendering from encoding lets it complete the repeated frame processing programmatically.

After checking video properties, the agent positions the video in Impress and starts the slideshow. Observations 143 and 144 show changing logo orientations. The task receives full credit after 147 decisions and 253 tool calls, including four notes. GUI-accessible scripting handles the repetitive work, and GUI playback verifies the result.
